Privacy Policy — No Guesswork Events

Effective: November 20, 2026

Who we are: No Guesswork Systems LLC (“we,” “us”), a Maryland limited liability company, 306 W Redwood St, Ste 201, Baltimore, MD 21201.

How to reach us about privacy: events@noguessworksystems.com.

No Guesswork Events (“the app”) helps a person plan an event — a wedding, a milestone birthday, a reunion — without a paid planner. This policy explains what we collect, from whom, why, who else sees it, how long we keep it, and what you can ask us to do. It is written to be read, not skimmed; the short version is at the end.

1. Three kinds of people use this app, and we collect different things from each

Hosts (the person planning the event)

  • Your email address, when you sign in. Sign-in is by a link or a code we email to that address; there is no password. Before the email is sent, Cloudflare's bot check runs on the sign-in form (section 4).
  • Whether you asked for offers and news. The sign-in form has a box, "Email me offers and news from No Guesswork," that starts unticked. If you tick it when you create your account, we store that you did, when, and the words you agreed to.
  • The email addresses of co-hosts you invite to an event, so we can send them the invitation.
  • Your studio or business name and role, if you enter them in your profile.
  • Your event plans: the event name, date, type, venue and town, guest count, budget figures, vendor names and contact details you enter, the food plan, shopping lists, lodging links you paste, notes, and uploaded photos.
  • Guest lists you import or type, which can include other people's names, and the dietary needs you record for them.
  • Your purchase of the One-Event Pass, if you buy one: which event it covers and the Stripe session that paid for it. We never see or store your card number.

Guests (someone replying to an invitation)

When you open an invitation link and reply, we store what you choose to give. Only your name and your answer are required; everything else is optional.

  • Your name and your answer (Yes / No / Maybe), so the host knows who is coming.
  • A meal choice, if you are coming, so the host can plan the food.
  • Allergies and diet: allergens picked from a list (peanut, tree nuts, milk, egg, fish, shellfish, soy, wheat or gluten, sesame), diet rules (such as gluten-free, dairy-free, halal, kosher, or no alcohol), and anything else you type, so the host can serve food that is safe for you.
  • Access needs, such as step-free or wheelchair access or an accessible seat, so the host can plan the way in and where you sit.
  • A plus-one (their name, meal, and needs) and how many children are coming with you, when the host allows them, so the host has a true headcount.
  • A phone number or email, so the host can reach you with day-of details.
  • Your mailing address, asked only when the host has turned this on and you are coming, so the host can mail thank-you notes or favors.
  • A note to the host.
  • For some events, which lodging you would prefer from options the host listed, or whether you will pick crabs at a crab feast, so the host can plan what to book or buy.

Who sees your reply. The host of the event sees everything above, and so does anyone the host shares the event's studio with (section 2) or adds as a co-host of that event. Other guests do not. An invitation shows other guests only how many people have said yes: never names, contact details, needs, or notes. The one exception is an invitation opened on the same device where the host's plan is saved, such as the host previewing it. That view can show the first names of up to two guests who said yes.

Allergies, diets, and access needs can reveal health information, and access needs may describe a disability. We treat those fields, and your phone number, email, mailing address, and note, as sensitive. They are stored only for the purpose listed above and shown only to the host of that event. They never appear on any public page and are never sent to analytics; the only analytics event a reply sends is your Yes / No / Maybe and the type of event. They are never shared with vendors unless the host chooses to pass them on. When you reply, the host gets a short email saying who answered and how (Yes, No, or Maybe), never your needs, contact details, or note.

You do not create an account, and we do not set an identity on you. Your reply is tied to the invitation code and an idempotency key your browser generates so a double-tap does not double-submit.

Guests sharing photos after the event

After the event, a guest can share photos from the invitation link.

  • What we store: the photo, the name you give with it, and the time you shared it, tied to the invitation code and your browser's key (the same key as your reply), and whether you chose to keep your photos private to the event. Photos are accepted only once the event has ended, by the host's end (or start) time in your phone's time zone, which your browser tells our server; the zone is used for that check and not stored.
  • Location and other hidden details are removed. Phone photos usually carry hidden details: where the photo was taken (GPS), the camera or phone model, and the time. Our server removes all of it before the photo is stored, by keeping only the picture itself and saving it as a new JPEG. The file you sent is never stored.
  • Who sees it: the host (and anyone the host shares the event's studio with, and the event's co-hosts) sees every photo with the name you gave. Other guests see a photo only after the host approves it, and they see the photo alone, without your name. The host can hide or delete any photo.
  • Sharing a photo, and what can't be undone. The upload screen says: "Approved photos can be shared by your host and other guests. Once someone shares a photo to Instagram or Facebook, deleting it here doesn't remove that post." Sharing means the app hands the photo to the person's own phone (its share sheet) and copies a caption with the event's name and, if the host turned one on, the event's hashtag; that person posts it from their own account, or doesn't. We never post anything, link any social account, or send photos to Instagram or Facebook ourselves. A photo someone has posted is outside this app: deleting it here, your own delete, the host's delete, and the 90-day deletion below do not remove that post.
  • Stopping sharing. You can switch on "Keep my photos private to this event": then no one gets a Share button on your photos, though guests can still see the ones the host approved. The host can also turn sharing off for any one photo, because the person in a picture isn't always the one who took it. Neither switch can pull back a post someone already made.
  • Colors. A phone photo's color profile is converted to standard colors (sRGB) and then removed with the rest of the hidden details, so the stored photo looks like the one you took.
  • Where it is kept: in a private storage area at Supabase that no browser can open directly. Each time a photo is shown, our server makes a link that stops working after five minutes.
  • Deleting it: you can delete your own photos from the same device you shared them from. From another device, write to us (section 6).
  • HEIC photos (an iPhone format) are not accepted; the app asks for a JPEG instead. This is a technical limit, not a privacy choice.

Vendors (a caterer, photographer, venue the host shares a brief with)

If a host shares a vendor brief with you, you receive a link that shows the event details the host chose to share — date, venue, headcount, timing, the host's requests — built from the host's current plan through a fixed list of vendor-safe fields. Guest names and guest dietary details are not in that list.

If you confirm back through that link, we store your confirmation.

Helpers (a friend or relative the host gives a party job)

If a host sends you your job by link ("you're bringing the stuffing"), the link shows who is asking, the event's name, date, start time and place, and only the jobs assigned to you, built from the host's current plan through a fixed list of fields. It shows no other guest's details. The host either shares the link themselves, from their own phone or email, or asks us to email it to you (section 3, "Email we send").

If you answer through that link ("I've got it" or "I can't", with an optional note), we store your answer and show it to the host. The only analytics event your answer sends is whether you said yes or no, never your note, and the same "turn analytics off" setting described in section 3 applies on that page.

Guests who ask the host a question

From your invitation you can ask the host a question, and the host can reply. We store your name, your questions, and the host's replies, as plain text. If you choose, we also store an email address you type and whether you ticked the box to be emailed; that box starts unticked. If you tick it, we email you when the host answers your question and when the host posts an update for everyone on the invitation. Each of those emails has a link that stops them; stopping also removes the email address you gave. When you ask a question, the host gets a short email saying that you asked, never the question itself.

Who sees it. The host of the event, anyone the host shares the event's studio with (section 2), and the event's co-hosts. Other guests never see your questions or your name. The host does not see your email address, only whether you asked to be emailed. You never see the host's email address.

Your host can see when you last opened your invite, but only once you have replied or asked a question from that device. Every other open is only counted: how many times the invitation was opened each day, and on how many devices. To count devices we keep a scrambled code (a salted hash) of a random number your browser makes, never your IP address.

Deleting it yourself. From the same device you asked from, you can delete your questions and the host's replies at once.

2. Where your data lives

  • On your device first. The app works without an account. Plans you make while signed out live only in your browser's storage on that device, and nothing leaves it except the lookups described in section 4.
  • In your account, when you sign in. Signed-in hosts' plans sync to our database so they survive a lost phone and can be shared. The database is hosted by Supabase in the United States. Each plan belongs to a studio, and database-level rules (row level security) allow only that studio's members to read or change it — our public API key cannot bypass them.
  • If two of your devices disagree, we do not silently overwrite either: a save against a plan another device changed is refused, kept on the device that made it, and you are told.

3. What we use it for

  • To run the app: show your plan, compute readiness, send invitations you ask us to send, build the briefs you share.
  • To take payment for the One-Event Pass, through Stripe's hosted checkout.
  • To fix what breaks: error reports go to Sentry with personal data disabled by default and a 10% sample of performance traces.
  • To learn which parts of the app help: product analytics go to PostHog with automatic click and form capture off, session recording off, and page views tracked by hand. A signed-in host is identified only by a one-way scrambled code (a hash) of the account's internal id, so your visits on different devices count as one person, never by your email, your name, or your business name. Name, email and phone fields are stripped before any event is sent. Events also carry the campaign tags in the link that first brought you to the app (such as utm_source), the name of the website that referred you (its host name only, never the page), and the pass price your device was shown.
  • Turning analytics off. You can turn analytics off any time in You & settings → Help improve the app, or with the first-open notice's "Turn this off." That stops everything the app sends to PostHog from that browser. Analytics events travel through our own server on the way to PostHog, unchanged; our server passes along your IP address so PostHog can tell which country a visit came from, as it could when the app sent to PostHog directly, and keeps no copy. When a pass is bought, our server also records the purchase in PostHog: the amount and whether it was the regular price or a test price, a scrambled code for the event, the same scrambled account code, and whether the event began from an invitation or a vendor brief. The server also records, under the same scrambled account code: when a pass payment is refunded or disputed (the amount, the currency, and whether it was all or part of the payment); each week-before reminder email we send you; and, when the mail service reports what happened to an email the app sent for you, the outcome (delivered, bounced, marked as spam, or delayed) and what kind of email it was (such as an invitation, a message or a helper's job). These never include the recipient's address, anyone's name, or the email's words. The server cannot see the switch in your browser, so it records these either way.
  • We do not sell personal data, we do not run advertising, and we do not share your data with data brokers.

Email we send

Every email below goes through Resend (section 4).

  • Sign-in. The link and code you asked for. These have no stop link, because you asked for each one.
  • Emails a host sends through the app: invitations, a message to one guest, a brief or message to a vendor, a helper's job, an approval request, and co-host invitations. Invitations come from "your host's name via No Guesswork." Each invitation and guest or vendor message has a "Stop emails about this event" link; after someone uses it, the app does not email that address about that event again.
  • Alerts to the host when a guest replies or asks a question, or a vendor answers a brief: who answered and what kind of answer, never what they wrote, at most one an hour for each event. The host can turn these off for each event in its guest list.
  • Emails to a guest who asked for them (section 1): the host's answers and the host's updates, each with a stop link.
  • Plan reminders to a host. We may email you reminders about your own plans, such as a note the week before your event. Each one has a link to stop plan reminders.
  • Offers and news, only if you ticked "Email me offers and news from No Guesswork" when you created your account. Each one has its own stop link. Stopping offers does not stop plan reminders, and stopping plan reminders does not stop offers.

Device notifications

If you turn on You & settings → Notifications on this device, that browser can show you a notification when a guest replies or asks a question, or a vendor answers your brief. It is off until you turn it on, on each device, and your browser asks your permission first. It is offered on computers and on Android phones, not on iPhone or iPad.

  • What we store: for each device you turn on, the web address your browser's push service gave it and the two keys used to lock the message to that browser, with your account and the time it was added and last worked. Nothing else about the device.
  • Who carries it: the push service of your browser's maker — Google (Chrome, and most Android browsers), Mozilla (Firefox), Apple (Safari on a Mac) or Microsoft (Edge). The message is encrypted to your browser, so that service carries it without being able to read it.
  • What it says: who answered and what kind of answer (for example, "Jordan replied Yes") and the event's name — never what anyone wrote. At most one an hour for each event, shared with the alert email, and none while the app is on your screen.
  • Turning it off: tap the same row on that device, or turn reply alerts off for one event in its guest list, which stops its emails and notifications together. We delete a device's record when you turn it off there, when its browser stops accepting messages, or when you delete your account.

5. How long we keep it

  • Your plans and account: until you delete them or ask us to (section 6). Deleting an event in the app deletes its database row.
  • Guest replies: we intend to delete replies 90 days after the event's date. The routine that does this exists and is run by hand today; it is not yet automatic, and this sentence will change when it is.
  • Guest questions, replies, and invitation opens: deleted 90 days after the event's date (or, without a date, 90 days after the last activity). The routine runs nightly where the database's scheduler is turned on; until the owner confirms it is running there, it is run by hand. The scrambled device codes are kept only for one day's count and deleted after two days. When the host deletes the event, its guest questions, the email addresses guests gave for answers, and its invitation opens are deleted with it, at once.
  • Guest photos: we intend to delete photos, and the record of who shared them, 90 days after the event's last day, and when the host deletes the event, its photos go within a day (they can't be opened from the moment the event is gone). A nightly job does this. Posts someone made on Instagram or Facebook are not ours to delete (section 1).
  • Pass purchases: kept as a record of what you bought; required for refunds and disputes. The receipt survives account deletion, with the link to your account removed (section 6).
  • Error reports and analytics: on Sentry's and PostHog's default retention for our plan; they hold no name or email from us.
  • Email we sent through Resend: on Resend's default retention.

6. What you can ask us to do

Write to events@noguessworksystems.com from the address on the account (or, for a guest, with the invitation code you replied to) and we will, within 30 days:

  • Tell you what we hold about you and send you a copy.
  • Correct it.
  • Delete it. For a guest that means your reply. A host can also delete their own account directly — see below.
  • Stop analytics for you (or just use ?noanalytics=1).

Deleting your account yourself. A signed-in host can delete their account in the app: You & settings → Your account → Delete my account…, then type DELETE to confirm. It happens at once and cannot be undone. It removes:

  • your sign-in identity;
  • every event that belongs only to you — the events in studios where you are the only member, and events you own outside any studio — with their guests' replies, vendor-brief links and vendors' confirmations, helper links and helpers' answers, guests' questions and your replies, invitation-open records, guests' shared photos (the files too), and event messages, so those invitation and brief links stop working;
  • studios where you are the only member, your studio memberships, and studio invitations you sent or received;
  • the files you uploaded to those events;
  • on that device, the app's copies of the account's events. Plans that were only ever saved on the device stay there until you remove them.

It keeps, and the app says so before you confirm:

  • payment receipts for any pass you bought, with the link to your account removed;
  • security and administrative records;
  • content in a studio you share with other people, which stays with them. In those studios your name is taken off the events you owned and off pinned messages.

It stops and tells you what to do first if you are the only owner of a studio other people still use (make someone else an owner), or if you uploaded files to an event someone else still has (transfer or remove them).

Signed-out plans never reached us; to delete them, remove them from the device. If you cannot sign in, write to us and we will do the deletion for you.

We will not treat you differently for asking. If you are in a US state with a privacy law that gives you these rights by statute (California, Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, and others), this is how you exercise them; we honor the same requests from everyone. We do not currently respond to browser "Do Not Track" signals, because the analytics described above do not track you across sites.

7. Children

The app is for adults planning events. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 13. A host may record a child's name and dietary needs on a guest list — that is the host's data about their guest, stored under the rules above, and a parent may ask us to remove it through section 6.

8. Security, honestly stated

Data in transit is encrypted (HTTPS). Database access is governed by row level security so one studio cannot read another's plans. Third-party API keys live on our server, never in the app you download. Payment is handled on Stripe's page, not ours. We do not claim certifications we do not hold. No system is perfectly secure; if we learn of a breach that affects you, we will tell you without unreasonable delay and as the law requires.

9. Changes

When this policy changes in a way that matters, we will put the new effective date at the top and, for hosts with an account, tell you in the app before the change takes effect.

10. The short version

  • Hosts: we keep your email and your plans so the app works; signed-out plans never leave your device.
  • Guests: your name, reply, meal and any dietary needs go only to the host. Photos you share have their location and other hidden details removed, and other guests see one only after the host approves it.
  • Vendors see a fixed, limited slice of the plan — never guests' details.
  • Payment happens on Stripe; we never see card numbers.
  • Analytics are minimal and opt-out; error reports carry no personal data.
  • Nothing is sold, nothing is advertised.
  • Email events@noguessworksystems.com to see, fix or delete your data.
